notes: Corrected: the supplied of in of which was moved from the relative to דבר. אשר is the bare direct object of that verb, with no object marker and no preposition of its own, so the preposition by which the English verb reaches it belongs to the verb's unit under rule 44, discontinuous under rule 25; rule 33's supplied function word is licensed by a noun's own case-function and does not reach a direct object, and rule 11 gives the relative no sense that licenses of. The same relative clause at v.14 is written bare.

The frame's that stands immediately after it shall come to pass, ahead of the as clause, so the frame keeps it (rule 45); the apodosis is opened by כן with no waw, so nothing else competes for the word.
